goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47 — The new call has no matching overload because the only helper requires a UserModel, leaving this class uncompilable.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's no matching overload for isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() in UsernameForm.java. Looking at the diff, UsernameForm.java at line 47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments. The diff shows UsernamePasswordForm.java adds a method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) that takes a UserModel parameter. However, UsernameForm extends AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator (based on the import context), and the no-argument version isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() could be inherited from a parent class or defined elsewhere not shown in this diff. The finding assumes this method doesn't exist, but we cannot verify this from the diff alone. More importantly, UsernamePasswordForm.java also calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without arguments in its authenticate method (line 113), suggesting there is indeed a no-argument version available. The finding appears to be incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/util/AuthenticatorUtils.java:35 — Move the re-authentication note and helper to a neutral owner because this generic utility now imports a browser authenticator, creating a package cycle and publicizing an internal key.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows AuthenticatorUtils.java (in package org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.util) now imports AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator from the browser package (line 34: 'import static org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.browser.AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH'). This creates a dependency from a utility package to a specific browser authenticator package. Additionally, the constant USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH was changed from 'protected' to 'public' (line 58 in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java) specifically to enable this cross-package access. This is a legitimate architectural concern - a generic utility class should not depend on a specific authenticator implementation. The finding correctly identifies this as a package coupling issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:291 — The two duplicated catch-Exception absence checks accept unrelated Selenium failures, so use assertThrows with NoSuchElementException as elsewhere in the suite.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to lines 291+ in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java where the test catches generic Exception to verify element absence. Looking at the diff, around lines 291-295 and 310-314, there are try-catch blocks catching 'Exception' with comments '// expected'. The finding suggests using assertThrows with NoSuchElementException instead, which is a valid test improvement suggestion. However, this is a test code style/robustness issue, not a bug - the test will still work correctly, it just might mask other unexpected exceptions. The suggestion to use assertThrows with NoSuchElementException is reasonable for test precision but doesn't represent a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47 — This call omits the newly required UserModel argument, so production compilation fails before the new tests can run.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for UsernameForm.java at line 47, the code shows `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`. The method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called without arguments. The finding claims this call 'omits the newly required UserModel argument', but examining the diff, the method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` is defined in UsernamePasswordForm.java (a different class), not in UsernameForm.java. The UsernameForm class likely inherits or has its own `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` method without parameters. The diff doesn't show any compilation error would occur - the no-argument version could be inherited from a parent class or defined elsewhere in UsernameForm. The finding incorrectly assumes the parameterized method from UsernamePasswordForm.java must be used here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 — Requiring a non-null user disables conditional passkey setup on every initial login and regresses the existing passkey flow.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that requiring a non-null user disables conditional passkey setup on initial login. However, examining the diff shows that `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` in UsernamePasswordForm.java returns true when `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. This method is used to determine when to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`. The change actually ensures passkeys are set up when a user IS present (re-authentication scenarios), not disabled. For initial login without a user, the existing flow in the `authenticate` method still handles passkeys setup in the `if (context.getUser() == null)` block. The tests in the diff confirm passkeys work correctly in both initial login and re-authentication scenarios.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:282 — This supposed password-only-user case disables passkeys realm-wide, so it never tests a user without a passkey while the realm supports passkeys.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` at the realm level, which disables passkeys for the entire realm rather than testing a scenario where the realm supports passkeys but a specific user doesn't have one registered. This is a valid test design concern - the test name suggests testing a user without a passkey, but the implementation disables the feature realm-wide. However, this could be intentional test design to verify behavior when passkeys are disabled, so it's not necessarily a bug but rather a potential gap in test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:53 — No added test submits a failing passkey during re-authentication, leaving this new error recovery and hidden-username state unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new error handling code in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse() at line 53 that calls AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context). This is new logic for handling passkey failures during re-authentication. Looking at the test files added, the tests cover successful passkey re-authentication scenarios (webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication) and password failures during re-authentication (webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey), but none of them specifically test a failing passkey authentication during re-authentication that would trigger the createErrorResponse path in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator. This is a valid observation about missing test coverage for newly added error handling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:294 — Catching every Exception lets unrelated WebDriver failures satisfy both new webauthn-absence assertions.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the test at line 294 (in the reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test) catches generic Exception to verify webauthn elements are not present. The code uses 'catch (Exception nsee)' which would catch any exception including unrelated WebDriver failures, not just NoSuchElementException. This is a valid test quality concern - the assertion could pass incorrectly if WebDriver fails for other reasons. However, this is a test code quality issue rather than a bug in the production code. The finding correctly identifies that catching generic Exception is too broad for this assertion pattern.
